newsitem.title: USA: New York Indian tribe makes Ellis Island claim.
newsitem.headline: New York Indian tribe makes Ellis Island claim.

text.p: An American Indian tribe has filed a motion laying claim to Ellis Island, adding a new twist to the dispute between New York and New Jersey over jurisdiction of the historic immigration site, officials said on Tuesday.

Last year the U.S. Supreme Court appointed a special master to consider New Jersey's legal claim to sovereignty of the island, which New York has claimed for two centuries, and a ruling is expected from the full court this summer.

But in papers filed with the New York State Attorney General last week, the Western Mohegan Tribe and Nation of New York claimed Ellis Island belonged to the tribe because the state of New York never bought it from them.
"Ellis Island is ours and so is the Statue of Liberty," said Sachem Ron Roberts, also known as Chief Golden Eagle. "We may consider giving it to New Jersey and give the statue back to France."
The tribe also claims the U.S. Supreme Court does not have jurisdiction in the matter and that it belongs in the Mohegan Confederated Native Court.
The New York Attorney General's office said the tribe had no right to claim Ellis Island because the tribe is not federally recognised by the U.S. Department of Interior.
"We are going to have this filing dismissed," said Mark Carey, a spokesman for Attorney General Dennis Vacco.

The special master, Columbia University law professor Paul Verkuil, has held a series of hearings on the competing claims in Washington and on Ellis Island, a major immigration processing centre from 1892 to 1943.

New Jersey claims that New York has sovereignty over only the island's original 2.7 acres (1 hectares) but that New Jersey has jurisdiction (and lucrative taxing powers) over the remaining 24 acres (9.7 hectares) of landfill added by the federal government, which owns the island.
